description: Identity genuinely unresolved. Delivered to the FAS after the 1969 war. When stripped for repainting in the late 1990s the civil registration N-86482 was found under the paint; which does not correspond to tail number 601; and the aircraft's ID plate had been deliberately destroyed; so the true identity cannot be established from the airframe. Compounding the problem; Castle Air Museum in California displays an A-26 that IT also identifies as "ex-FAS 601". On display in the Plaza de la Aviación since 2001. The tail number is recorded here as FAS 601 because that is how the airframe is universally referenced; but it should be treated as a worn marking of uncertain validity; not a confirmed identity. Variant (A-26B / A-26C) not established — left blank rather than guessed.

Ex-Israeli Ouragan; airframe series 381; delivered to the FAS on 2 September 1975; retired in the second half of the 1980s. Was the personal aircraft of General (r) Juan Rafael Bustillo; former FAS commander; callsign "01". A repaired bullet strike is visible low on the left fuselage from the incident in which Colonel Óscar Nelson Bolaños "Master" was wounded in the foot in the early 1980s. On display in the Plaza de la Aviación.

Airframe series 03; Marboré II engines; delivered to the FAS from Israel on 10 February 1974 as part of the programme that brought jets into the Rama Aérea. On display in the Plaza de la Aviación since 2001.

Airframe number 13275; delivered to the FAS on 5 January 1981 and flown by the Escuela de Aviación Militar. On display in the Plaza de la Aviación since 2001. The FAS museum website styles the type "Rallye 235GTA".

Airframe serial recorded only as 27-2xxx. Operated in El Salvador by the Instituto Geográfico Nacional; then transferred to the Ministerio de Obras Públicas and finally to the Autoridad de Aviación Civil in 2003. On display in the Plaza de la Aviación. Photo credit Steve Homewood.

Built 1968 and sent straight to combat in Vietnam as 68-7973; flew with the 176th Tactical Air Support Squadron; Wisconsin ANG; from 1975 and the 169th Tactical Fighter Squadron; Illinois ANG; from 1981. Delivered to the FAS on 30 January 1985. Withdrawn after damage in a forced landing on El Zapote beach; La Paz; on 9 January 2013. On display in the Plaza de la Aviación since January 2023 — the most recent addition to the Plaza. Specifically an OA-37B forward air control variant.
